My land is about 5 mu, flat and good, like everyone else's here in Quzhou. I've been farming it since I was young. My mother grew wheat and corn on this same ground, and so did her mother. I don't have schooling but I know this land and I know what sells at the grain station.

Wheat goes in in October, corn goes in right after the wheat comes out in June. That's the whole year. Same as my neighbors, same as the people across the road. I'm not going to try cotton or something strange — I'm 55 and I farm alone since my husband can't do heavy work anymore.

For seeds I go to Lao Wang's shop in the village. He sells the improved wheat variety — I've used it the past three years, it's good, no lodging. For corn I get hybrid seeds, the kind everyone switched to years ago. I tried saving my own corn seed once when I was younger, the yield was terrible, I won't do that again.

Fertilizer — I put compound fertilizer down when I plant, then urea when the wheat is growing in spring. Maybe more than I should, but I worry about yellow plants. Corn gets urea at topdressing when it's knee-high. Water is the hard part. My electric pump on the well is old but it still works. Wheat needs more — I irrigate before the ground freezes, again at jointing, again at heading. For corn just twice unless the summer is very dry. The water table has been dropping every year, I know this, but I can't change it.

For tillage, I hire a tractor to do rotary tillage before wheat planting. For corn I don't bother tilling after harvest — just plant directly, saves money and the soil has enough loose straw on it.

Near my house I keep a small patch, half a mu or less, for tomatoes, beans, and cucumbers. Mostly for ourselves to eat, maybe a little to sell in the village.
